questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to choose some place I had never been before, where I had ample opportunity to explore new cultures, meet new people, and study environmental discourses under different paradigms.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: With help from mobility officers from the program, this was much easier than I expected.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance in organizing my Dichiarazione di Presenza, an extension of my study visa.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Luckily, i was guaranteed dorm housing in Padova, otherwise it would have been impossible to find accomodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The dorms are not very nice and have terrible rules. While it is a good alternative to not having housing at all, its definitely recommended to find private accommodation if possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: My courses were pretty much prescribed for me based on the program requirements, so I just registered for the courses they told me to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Department secretaries and professors were all very helpful in finding and registering for the right courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful, I did not miss out on any classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have no advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The master's level courses were challenging and rigorous in a way that pushed me to do my best work.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It involved much less group work than at UCPH, and the classes were smaller.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mountain River Morphology and Restoration
Forest Transportation

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Forest Hydrology and Erosion Control
Market-Based Instruments for Ecosystem Services
Guidelines to Develop your Master's Thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Mountain River Morphology and Restoration because it gave us ample opportunity to explore the Dolomites and do field work.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lost of good erasmus events and organized activites.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not sure there was too much organized directly through the institution, but students organized their own sports, music, and other activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Volleyball is very popular here and a great way to make friends!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely travel to the Dolomites if you like hiking and nature. Otherwise, there are many cool places to visit such as Florence, Rome, Milan, Cinque Terre, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Less easy than in Copenhagen, as less people speak English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn Italian.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier and the times shops/restaurants close and open

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the food and aperitivo culture. The lifestyle in Italian cities can be quite relaxed and fun.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Start looking for accommodation ASAP!! Housing is very difficult to find.
2. Learn some Italian if you can.
3. Attend lectures as often as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everywhere is accessible by train and I ended up spending a lot of money on rail transit. Make sure to register with TrenItalia CartaFreccia and try to travel as much as possible while saving what you can.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was graduating with a degree from a foreign country after working very hard to pass all the classes, learn as much as I could from my professors, and do the best work possible.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was communication with people who don't speak English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
